description: Known answers for the Unicode NFKC normalisation a passphrase goes through before it becomes a bundle key (SWR-MG-02, NP-SOUP-RUST-001). Every answer is from the Unicode Standard's decomposition mappings and the NFKC algorithm (UnicodeData.txt, UAX #15), written by hand, not produced by the crate under test. Run by the Rust core against its own function and by Kotlin, Swift, C# and the web through their binding, so the corpus checks the crate's tables AND that each platform hands the core the same code points (the outside-the-BMP cases are where a UTF-16 or modified-UTF-8 boundary would go wrong). A case's input is `padding` followed by `input`; its secret is the UTF-8 of `padding` followed by `expected`, as hex. The crate's Unicode version is 17.0.0; a change to it that changes any answer here is a change to every sealed passphrase bundle.

cases.name: angstrom sign is the Latin A with ring
ohm sign is the Greek capital omega
kelvin sign is the Latin K
e and a combining acute compose
vulgar fraction one half uses the fraction slash
halfwidth katakana ka and the voiced mark compose to ga
hangul jamo compose to a syllable
a, dot above, dot below reorders and composes
a, dot below, dot above composes the same
mathematical bold capital A (outside the BMP)
mathematical bold digit zero (outside the BMP)
mathematical double-struck digit one (outside the BMP)
an emoji is unchanged (outside the BMP)

exact.name: six ligatures count as twelve letters, so the floor is met
twelve emoji are twelve characters, not twenty-four

tooShort.name: six emoji are six characters, not twelve
six e-acute written as two code points each are six characters after normalising
six mathematical bold letters are six characters
